title: Research sprint goal: Research: Linux host configuration management and hardening by a pull agent
goal: The sprint goal's open questions are answered from official sources (each project's own docs; kb tools first, live docs for the gaps) and written as kb facts and gap entries through the kb skills. Open (pack coverage none, weak, or a false good whose cited lines do not answer it, 2026-10-11): (1) CIS Benchmark Level 1 and Level 2 server profiles for Debian, Ubuntu, Alpine and AlmaLinux: which families have one, version, machine-readable form; (2) OpenSCAP with the SCAP Security Guide profiles each family ships, and Lynis where no SSG content exists (Alpine); (3) nftables ruleset files, sets and atomic load with nft -f; (4) auditd rules under /etc/audit/rules.d, augenrules, immutable mode; (5) sshd_config options CIS grades and sshd -T; (6) chrony and systemd-timesyncd; (7) automatic upgrades off (apt-daily timers, unattended-upgrades, dnf-automatic) and package pins by snapshot date (snapshot.debian.org, snapshot.ubuntu.com), point release (AlmaLinux vault, Alpine vX.Y) or index hash; (8) Docker secrets under /run/secrets, never environment variables; (9) WireGuard hub-and-spoke: wg-quick, AllowedIPs at the hub, PersistentKeepalive; (10) cloudflared tunnel replicas and Cloudflare Access for an SSH admin path; (11) Incus machine containers and VMs as a test bed (images, launch, exec, snapshot); (12) a pull agent: static binary fetching a git main, refusing a backwards version, idempotent typed steps with check, apply and dry-run (extend prior-art/drift-detection.md, which covers Puppet noop and Chef InSpec); (13) dead-man heartbeat monitors on a second provider. Already answered in the kb: none.
